source_name: TEB SHA Kosovo — Çmimorja / tarifat e përgjithshme
why_relevant: Another mandated bank tariff publication (commission types by account/card/transfer). The 2017-dated file surfaced in search indicates historical versions remain accessible — useful for building a fee time series.

source_name: GAP Institute — 'Mbrojtja e konsumatorëve në sektorin bankar' (Consumer protection in the banking sector)
why_relevant: Think-tank analysis of banking-sector consumer protection in Kosovo: complaint trends, fee transparency gaps and regulatory shortcomings. Also a pointer to the underlying official data series and legal acts.

source_name: INDEP — 'Mbrojtja e konsumatorëve në Kosovë: standardet, rregullat dhe politikat'
why_relevant: Maps Kosovo's consumer-protection institutional architecture and EU-acquis alignment; a pointer source that names the responsible bodies, laws and complaint routes to snowball from.

source_name: Kallxo.com (BIRN Kosovo) — 'Rriten ankesat ndaj bankave në Kosovë' and related investigations
why_relevant: Investigative outlet that extracts and contextualises BQK complaint figures (e.g. 353 complaints in 2014 rising to 927 in 2018) and documents consumer grievances — missing contracts, high fees, phantom withdrawals — that official summaries do not itemise.

source_name: Shoqata për Mbrojtjen e Konsumatorëve të Kosovës (Kosovo Consumer Protection Association)
why_relevant: Civil-society consumer association that publicises grievances and names traders/banks harming consumers; its main visible publishing channel appears to be social media rather than an institutional website.

source_name: Radio Evropa e Lirë (RFE/RL Kosovo) — banking fee coverage
why_relevant: Broadcast journalism on bank fee increases ('Bankat shtrenjtojnë tarifat për shërbime?!'); useful as an early-warning channel for tariff changes and public reaction, and for archival coverage predating current bank websites.

source_name: IMF Kosovo country page (Article IV, program reviews, staff reports)
why_relevant: Primary analytic source on Kosovo's banking and payment system: Article IV staff reports, selected issues papers, SBA/RSF review documents. Discusses credit-to-GDP, NPLs, supervision gaps, crisis management and payment-system modernisation with frankness domestic sources avoid. 2026 Article IV concluded; 2024 Article IV concluded alongside 3rd SBA/RSF reviews.

source_name: IMF Kosovo Financial Sector Stability Review (FSSR) technical assistance report
why_relevant: FSAP-equivalent deep dive for a non-FSAP-mandatory jurisdiction: supervision, systemic risk oversight, crisis management, financial safety net, and payment/settlement infrastructure. Highest-density single document on Kosovo banking-system weaknesses. Notably, CBK republishes it in Serbian, giving a bilingual terminology anchor.

source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports — Kosovo (country code XK) financial sector documents
why_relevant: Holds Kosovo Financial Sector Assessment, ROSC accounting/auditing updates, Financial Sector Strengthening Project appraisal/implementation docs, Public Finance Review, and Country Partnership Framework reviews (e.g. Report No. 167914-XK). Project documents often disclose bank-level and supervisory detail not otherwise published.

source_name: World Bank Kosovo documents in Serbian (Srpski) — e.g. Kosovo Pregled javnih finansija
why_relevant: Confirms the World Bank publishes Kosovo material in local languages; these translations are the cleanest bilingual glossary for financial-sector terminology (bankarski sektor, nekvalitetni krediti/NPL, adekvatnost kapitala) used later in sr-language searching of bank disclosures.

source_name: BQK/CBK statistics hub (Rreth statistikave) — national aggregator of bank-level returns
why_relevant: The de-facto aggregator for Kosovo banking data: monetary & financial statistics and external-sector statistics are legally CBK's responsibility, compiled from commercial banks, MFIs, insurers and pension funds. Underlies every IMF/World Bank Kosovo series, so it is the upstream node for the whole aggregator layer.

source_name: BQK Financial Stability Report / Izveštaj o Finansijskoj Stabilnosti (multilingual archive)
why_relevant: Serial with numbered editions (No. 20, No. 21) published in Albanian, Serbian and English under stable wp-content paths — a predictable, machine-harvestable archive and the best bilingual anchor for stability/risk terminology.

source_name: BQK CBK Annual Reports archive (Raporti Vjetor) — historical PDF series
why_relevant: Continuous annual series back to ~2009 with sector-level balance sheets, licensed-institution lists and payment-system statistics. Critically, the site was re-platformed: older files sit under /repository/docs/... and newer ones under /wp-content/uploads/2024/11/..., so pre-migration URLs are exactly the class of link that needs web-archive recovery.

source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine + CDX API (recovery layer for removed Kosovo bank/IR disclosures)
why_relevant: The only practical way to recover Kosovo bank IR pages, quarterly disclosures and pre-migration BQK PDFs after site redesigns (bqk-kos.org moved from /repository/docs to /wp-content; commercial banks routinely rotate 'Raporte financiare' pages). CDX API enables systematic diffing of what a bank used to publish versus what it publishes now.

source_name: archive.today / archive.ph mirror
why_relevant: Secondary web archive that captures JS-heavy pages and press releases the Wayback Machine misses, and is often the only surviving copy of deleted Kosovo bank news posts. Complementary redundancy for the archive layer.

source_name: Fitch Ratings — Kosovo sovereign and Kosovo bank issuer ratings
why_relevant: Fitch is the agency that gave Kosovo its first-ever sovereign rating (BB-, affirmed with stable outlook; affirmations reported Oct 2024 and Mar 2025) and also rates individual Kosovo banks (e.g. ProCredit Bank Kosovo at BB+). Rating action commentaries are the densest third-party credit narrative on Kosovo banks available.

source_name: Rating-aggregator mirrors: Cbonds, SeeNews, TradingEconomics ratings list, countryeconomy.com
why_relevant: Free, structured mirrors of rating actions that bypass the agencies' registration walls and give machine-readable history of Kosovo's sovereign rating and outlook changes; SeeNews additionally covers Kosovo bank-level corporate news in a regional feed.

source_name: EBRD Transition Report — Kosovo country assessments (annual series)
why_relevant: Annual, comparable, country-level assessment of Kosovo's financial sector reform: bank capitalisation, NPL trend, Law on Banks progress, credit-market development. Long back-run (2013 through 2024-25) makes it a ready-made time series of qualitative reform scoring, plus EBRD Country Strategy adds bank-level project detail.

source_name: European Commission enlargement package — Kosovo Country Report (Ch.17 economic & monetary policy, Ch.4 free movement of capital, Ch.9 financial services)
why_relevant: Annual, chaptered assessment of Kosovo's alignment with the EU financial-services acquis and payment-services legislation — the best structured tracker of regulatory change affecting banks and payment providers. Companion Economic Reform Programme assessments add macro-financial detail.

source_name: ecoi.net — country-of-origin document archive (mirrors EU/UN Kosovo reports)
why_relevant: Independent mirror that preserves EU enlargement and other institutional Kosovo reports with stable local file URLs (e.g. kosovo-report-2025.pdf), useful when the Commission rotates its download tokens. Acts as a de-facto archive of official documents.

source_name: BIS central bankers' speeches archive — Kosovo (CBK Governor speeches)
why_relevant: BIS permanently archives CBK governors' speeches in English (e.g. Fehmi Mehmeti on 2021 growth and the banking system), preserving statements that later vanish from bqk-kos.org and providing an English rendering of Albanian-language remarks — a genuine translation layer for central-bank communication.

source_name: Riinvest Institute (Instituti për Hulumtime Zhvillimore Riinvest)
why_relevant: Kosovo's oldest economic think tank (since 1995), 100+ research reports, with recurring work on access to finance, credit costs and the banking sector. Publishes in Albanian and English and often reproduces bank data that is otherwise scattered — a domestic aggregator/interpreter layer.

source_name: MPRA / RePEc / IDEAS — academic working papers on Kosovo banking
why_relevant: Open academic aggregator holding papers such as a history of the development of Kosovo's banking sector; academic papers frequently cite and reproduce bank-level figures from CBK reports that are no longer online, effectively acting as a secondary archive plus a source of long-run series.

source_name: Monitor.al and regional Albanian-language financial press (aggregating Kosovo bank results)
why_relevant: Albanian financial magazine that regularly aggregates and interprets Kosovo banking-sector results ('Bankat, një nga sektorët më solidë të ekonomisë në Kosovë'), often summarising CBK figures faster than the CBK's own English editions appear — useful early-warning and Albanian-terminology corpus.

source_name: RBI — Quarterly / Semi-Annual Financial Reports (PDF series)
why_relevant: Quarterly reports carry the same SEE segment disclosure at higher frequency; observed PDF naming pattern is highly regular and machine-collectable, giving a quarterly time series of Kosovo-relevant group data.

source_name: NLB Group — Investor Relations
why_relevant: NLB d.d. (LJSE-listed, GDRs) owns NLB Banka sh.a. Prishtinë, the ~3rd largest bank in Kosovo. NLB's IR pack is unusually granular by market: per-country P&L, loan/deposit growth, market share, digital-user and channel metrics — often more detailed on Kosovo than the local subsidiary publishes.

source_name: NLB Group — quarterly investor presentation PDFs (nlb.si year-partitioned archive)
why_relevant: Stable, predictable PDF URL scheme by year and quarter, giving a long back-series of NLB Group presentations containing Kosovo market slides (loan growth, market share, digital adoption). Ideal for automated time-series collection.

source_name: Ljubljana Stock Exchange SEOnet — NLB d.d. regulated disclosures
why_relevant: Statutory disclosure channel for NLB d.d.; inside information, results announcements and material subsidiary events (including Kosovo) land here first and in machine-retrievable form with timestamps.
